newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Peasant leader killed in Colombian capital.
newsitem.headline: Peasant leader killed in Colombian capital.

text.p: A peasant leader who helped organise last year's protests of a U.S.-backed drug crop eradication programme in southern Colombia was shot and killed on Friday in the capital Bogota, police said.
They said two gunmen entered the office of 38-year-old Victor Julio Garzon shortly after 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT) and shot him four times before fleeing on a motorcycle.

Garzon, secretary-general of a farm workers union known as Fensuagro, led mass demonstrations late last year against the government's aerial spraying of illicit coca crops in the southern provinces of Caqueta and Guaviare.
Farm workers in the impoverished south staged the protests because coca -- the raw material for cocaine -- is one of the few cash crops that they can eke out a living with.
At least six other labour leaders and peasants associated with the protests have been killed in recent weeks, according to unions and peasant organisations.

In Magdalena province, a banana-growing region of northern Colombia, at least six people were dragged out of their homes near the town of Fundacion late on Thursday and killed by suspected right-wing gunmen, police said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, but police said the killings appeared similar to others committed in the region by right-wing death squads. At least 25 people have been killed so far this year.

Fundacion is located near the town of Aracataca, where Colombia's Nobel laureate Gabriel Garcia Marquez was born 70 years ago. The world-renowned author of "One Hundred Years of Solitude" has cited Colombia's seemingly uncontrolled levels of violence as one of the reasons he has decided to live in self-imposed exile in Mexico.
Colombia, a country torn by endemic levels of political and drug-related bloodshed, has the highest murder rate in Latin America, according to a World Bank report released this week.
